interface.title: Immune Cell Population Analysis (Loblaw Bio – miraclib clinical trial)
interface.field: Immunology / clinical-trial immune profiling (cytometry-style cell population counts)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and reporting of a finished trial dataset: exploratory comparison, hypothesis testing and cohort summary
interface.what_it_is_for: A Streamlit dashboard that turns raw counts of five immune cell populations per blood sample into per-sample relative frequencies, a responder vs non-responder statistical comparison you can filter by cohort, and a baseline (time = 0) cohort summary, each downloadable as CSV.

data.note: The bundled trial data loads when the page opens. There is no sign-in, upload or demo button. Part 2 covers about 10,500 samples × 5 populations (part2_frequencies.csv, 2.7 MB). The default Part 3 cohort (melanoma / miraclib / PBMC) has 993 responders and 975 non-responders. The Part 4 baseline subset has 656 samples, 656 subjects and 2 projects (prj1 384, prj3 272). The B cell average for melanoma male responders at baseline is 10206.15 (n = 485 samples).

tree.general: Find out how immune cell make-up varies between samples and whether any cell population predicts response to a treatment
tree.specific: Answer Bob Loblaw's questions about the miraclib trial: sample composition, which populations predict response, and the baseline cohort picture

features.name: Cascading cohort filter with group-comparison boxplot and statistics table
features.general: Choose a subgroup with linked dropdowns. The tool then draws side-by-side distributions of each measured variable for two outcome groups and tests each variable with a primary nonparametric test (FDR-corrected and flagged), a parametric test shown for reference only, and an effect size. It warns when the subgroup is empty.
features.specific: Pick condition, treatment and sample_type. Treatment options narrow to the chosen condition (healthy offers only 'none'). Read the responder vs non-responder boxplots per population and the statistics table: Mann-Whitney U p (primary, BH-FDR-corrected as mannwhitney_p_fdr and driving the significant_fdr_0.05 checkbox column), Welch t p (reference only, not corrected or flagged) and rank-biserial r. Download the comparison as CSV.
steps: Choose condition (melanoma / carcinoma / healthy)
Choose treatment, from options limited to that condition
Choose sample_type (PBMC / WB)
Read the boxplots and the chart title naming the cohort, or the 'No samples match' warning
Read mannwhitney_p_fdr and the significance flag for the decision, with rank_biserial_r for effect size and welch_ttest_p for reference
Press 'Download this comparison (CSV)'
serves_tasks: Compare the two outcome groups' distributions for each population in the main cohort
Read the significance tests with multiple-testing correction and effect size, noting which test carries the decision
Repeat the comparison in other subgroups

features.name: Per-item composition table with optional single-item filter and CSV export

features.specific: The Part 2 frequency table (sample, total_count, population, count, percentage). 'Filter to a single sample (optional)' is a type-ahead selectbox. 'Download this table (CSV)' exports the full or filtered table as part2_frequencies.csv.
steps: Open the table with all samples
Type a sample ID in the filter and pick it
Read that sample's five population percentages
Press 'Download this table (CSV)' to export the current view
Pick 'All samples' to clear the filter
serves_tasks: Express each population as a share of the sample's total cells
Inspect the composition of one chosen sample

features.name: Interactive data grid (sort, search, column visibility, number format, fullscreen)
features.general: Explore a large results table in place: sort by any column, find a value, hide columns you don't need, change how numbers are shown, and expand to full screen.
features.specific: The Streamlit dataframe grid used for the Part 2 frequencies and the Part 3 statistics. Header click sorts. The toolbar has Search with result count and next/previous, Show/hide columns checkboxes, and Fullscreen. Each column menu offers Sort, Statistics, Format (e.g. Scientific), Autosize, Pin and Hide.

features.name: Grouped boxplot with hover statistics, legend toggling and zoom/export toolbar
features.general: Inspect distributions per category split by group. Hover for quartiles and fences, hide a group from the legend, zoom and reset, and save the figure as an image. Bringing a hidden group back was unreliable.
features.specific: The Plotly boxplot of % of total cells per population, coloured by response (no/yes). Hover shows min, lower fence, q1, median, q3, upper fence and max. Clicking a legend swatch (not the label text) hides that response group. Restoring it was inconsistent: in the exploring run, further legend clicks, a double-click, Zoom in and Reset axes left it hidden until a tab switch re-rendered the chart; in the replay, Zoom in brought it back. The toolbar has Zoom in/out, Autoscale, Reset axes and 'Download plot as a PNG'.
steps: Hover a box to read its summary statistics
Click a legend swatch to hide one group (restoring it may need a tab switch)
Press Zoom in, then Reset axes
Press the camera icon to download the PNG

screens_never_reached: A responder comparison for treatment 'none' with any condition other than healthy: the treatment list only offers 'none' for healthy, and healthy has no responder/non-responder samples, so the page only shows the 'No samples match this combination of filters.' warning (screens/024.webp).
A per-sample composition chart: picking a single sample filters the table only. The bar chart always shows the average across all samples (screens/010.webp).
A Part 4 view with other cohort settings: the baseline subset is fixed to melanoma / PBMC / miraclib at time = 0 and has no filters.
not_done: Choosing between Mann-Whitney U and Welch's t-test: there is no method selector. Both p-values appear side by side in one table, and the FDR correction and significance flag apply only to Mann-Whitney (the primary test).
The grid toolbar's own 'Download as CSV' icon (Part 2 table) did not produce a file in this headless browser (screens/047.webp). The app's 'Download this table (CSV)' buttons did work.

Restoring the hidden 'no' group from the legend: after the first click hid it (screens/031.webp), several more single clicks and a double-click did not bring it back (screens/033.webp, screens/034.webp, screens/036.webp). It only reappeared after switching tabs re-rendered the chart (screens/051.webp). The replay instead saw Zoom in bring it back, so this behaviour is inconsistent.
Box-select zoom by dragging on the boxplot had no visible effect (screens/032.webp). The toolbar Zoom in button did work.
I did not try the column menu's Statistics submenu, Pin column or Autosize.
